newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sour crudes weak, talk centers on West Coast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sour crudes weak, talk centers on West Coast.

text.p: U.S. sour crude prices slumped Tuesday on continued fundamental pressures and talk supplies of West Coast heavies may be shipped to the U.S. Gulf.
Traders however, tempered such talk of possible West Coast shipments, noting the incompatibility of bringing the crudes to the Gulf.
"There are a lot of problems with the West Coast crudes coming here, there is the difference in the metals content and such, it's not something I see," said one Gulf crude trader.
Another trader downplayed the rumors, saying "that stuff out of California is ugly, ugly stuff. Quality has to enter into this somehow."
Speculation on the possible West Coast connection to the weak state of sour prices was a result of a refiner incident at Tosco Corp's Martinez, California refinery.

Martinez was hit by a fire in late January, knocking out a hydrocracker for up to 10 weeks, leaving the refiner unable to take delivery of all its heavy crude intake. The excess crude has not found other West Coast outlets due to heavy refinery maintenance schedules, traders noted.
Traders said West Texas Sour Midland was sold at a $2.30 and $2.35 discount to the West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark on Tuesday.
